solution: Equation: \(\vec u\cdot\vec v=u_1v_1+u_2v_2\). Substitution: \(\vec u\cdot\vec v=5(12)+3(4)=60+12=72\). Answer: \(72\).

Equation: \(\ln(x^2-2)=\ln((2x-3)^2-2)\), with both arguments positive. Algebra: \(x^2-2=(2x-3)^2-2\Rightarrow x^2=(2x-3)^2\Rightarrow x=1\text{ or }x=3\). Domain check: \(x=1\) gives \(x^2-2=-1\), invalid; \(x=3\) is valid. Answer: \(x=3\).
Substitution in the remainder theorem: \(3^4-k^2(3)+3-k=4\). Algebra: \(81-3k^2+3-k=4\Rightarrow3k^2+k-80=0\). The sum of the roots is \(-b/a=-1/3\). Answer: \(-\dfrac13\).
Equation: \(y=t^2-2t\). Completing the square: \(y=(t-1)^2-1\). Since \((t-1)^2\ge0\), the minimum is attained at \(t=1\). Answer: \(-1\).
Equation: \(f(x)=3\lvert\sin(\pi x+1/3)\rvert-5\). Since \(\lvert\sin u\rvert\) has period \(\pi\), require \(\pi(x+T)+1/3-(\pi x+1/3)=\pi\). Algebra: \(\pi T=\pi\Rightarrow T=1\). Answer: \(1\).

Equation: \(\log_3(x+11)-\log_3(x+3)=2\), with \(x>-3\). Substitution: \(\log_3\left(\dfrac{x+11}{x+3}\right)=2\Rightarrow\dfrac{x+11}{x+3}=9\). Algebra: \(x+11=9x+27\Rightarrow x=-2\), which satisfies the domain. Answer: \(-2\).

Equation: \(\tan\theta=\left\lvert\dfrac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1m_2}\right\rvert\). Substitution: \(m_1=3/5\), \(m_2=-1/2\), so \(\tan\theta=\left\lvert\dfrac{-1/2-3/5}{1-3/10}\right\rvert=11/7\). Algebra: \(\theta=\arctan(11/7)\approx57.53^\circ\). Answer: \(57.53^\circ\).

Equation: \(f(x)=f(-x)\). Substitution: \(x^k+8x^2-32x^4=(-x)^k+8x^2-32x^4\), so \(x^k=(-x)^k\) for every real \(x\). Algebra: \(k\) must be even; with \(1<k<17\), \(k=2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16\). Sum: \(2(1+2+\cdots+8)=72\). Answer: \(72\).

Equation: \(S=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{2n+2}{3^n}\). Let \(r=1/3\). Substitution: \(S=2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}nr^n+2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}r^n=2\dfrac{r}{(1-r)^2}+2\dfrac{r}{1-r}\). Algebra: \(S=2\left(\dfrac34\right)+2\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac52\). Answer: \(\dfrac52\).

Equation for parallel-plane distance: \(d=\dfrac{|k-8|}{\sqrt{1^2+2^2+3^2}}=10\). Algebra: \(\dfrac{|k-8|}{\sqrt{14}}=10\Rightarrow |k-8|=10\sqrt{14}\Rightarrow k=8\pm10\sqrt{14}\). Answer: \(8+10\sqrt{14}\) or \(8-10\sqrt{14}\).
Equation: choose 5 items from 8 types with repetition. Substitution into combinations with repetition: \(N=\binom{8+5-1}{5}=\binom{12}{5}\). Algebra: \(N=792\). Answer: \(792\).

Substitution using principal inverse branches: \(\sec^{-1}(-2/\sqrt3)=5\pi/6\) and \(\csc^{-1}(-2)=-\pi/6\). Algebra: \(\cot(5\pi/6-\pi/6)=\cot(2\pi/3)=\dfrac{-1/2}{\sqrt3/2}=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{3}\). Answer: \(-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{3}\).
Equation: \(a+bi=(2-i)^2+(1+i)^2\). Substitution: \((2-i)^2=3-4i\) and \((1+i)^2=2i\), so \(a+bi=3-2i\). Algebra: \(\lvert a+bi\rvert=\sqrt{3^2+(-2)^2}=\sqrt{13}\). Answer: \(\sqrt{13}\).

Equation: \(\tan(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)=\dfrac{a+b+c-abc}{1-ab-bc-ca}\). Substitution: \(a=1/3,b=1/5,c=1/9\) gives numerator \(86/135\) and denominator \(118/135\). Algebra: \(\tan(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)=\dfrac{86/135}{118/135}=\dfrac{43}{59}\). Answer: \(\dfrac{43}{59}\).
Rationalize: \(\sqrt{n^2+kn+5}-\sqrt{n^2+3n+7}=\dfrac{(k-3)n-2}{\sqrt{n^2+kn+5}+\sqrt{n^2+3n+7}}\). Divide by \(n\): the limit is \((k-3)/2\). Algebra: \((k-3)/2=4\Rightarrow k=11\). Answer: \(11\).

Let \(B=\angle ABD\). The angle-bisecting diagonal is \(BC\), so \(BC/AD=4/3\). Set \(BC=4q,AD=3q\). Since the diagonals are perpendicular bisectors, \(15^2=(2q)^2+(3q/2)^2\Rightarrow q=6\), hence \(BC=24,AD=18\). In the right triangle formed by half-diagonals, \(\tan(B/2)=(AD/2)/(BC/2)=3/4\), so \(B\approx73.74^\circ\). Opposite angles \(B\) and \(\angle ACD\) are equal, so the answer is \(74^\circ\).

Set \(A=(0,0),B=(1,0),C=(\cos24^\circ,\sin24^\circ)\). The angle data give \(E=\lambda C=B+t(\cos153^\circ,\sin153^\circ)\) and \(D=(d,0)=C+u(\cos228^\circ,\sin228^\circ)\). Solving the two line equations gives \(E\approx(0.533672,0.237606)\) and \(D\approx(0.547318,0)\). Substitution in the dot-product angle formula: \(\cos\angle EDC=\dfrac{(E-D)\cdot(C-D)}{|E-D||C-D|}\), so \(\angle EDC\approx45.287^\circ\). Answer: \(45.3^\circ\).
Equation: \(\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{x^2-3x}{3x^2-5}\). Divide numerator and denominator by \(x^2\): \(\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{1-3/x}{3-5/x^2}=\dfrac13\). Answer: \(\dfrac13\).
Complete the squares: \(-16(x+1)^2+9(y-3)^2+144=0\Rightarrow16(x+1)^2-9(y-3)^2=144\). This is the standard hyperbola form \(\dfrac{(x+1)^2}{9}-\dfrac{(y-3)^2}{16}=1\). Answer: \(\text{Hyperbola}\).

Equation: \(\sin2\theta=k\). Algebra: \((\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2=\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta+2\sin\theta\cos\theta=1+\sin2\theta=1+k\). Since \(\theta\) is acute, the sum is positive. Answer: \(\sqrt{1+k}\).

Square the equation \(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=1-y\): \(x^2+y^2=(1-y)^2\Rightarrow x^2+2y=1\). Substitute \(2y=-1-x\) from \(x+2y=-1\): \(x^2-x-2=0\Rightarrow x=2,-1\). Both satisfy the unsquared equation; sum \(=2+(-1)=1\). Answer: \(1\).

Substitution in \(y=f(x-1)\): the point \( (2,3)\) gives \(f(1)=3\). Invert the graph: \(f(1)=3\Rightarrow f^{-1}(3)=1\), so \( (3,1)\) lies on \(y=f^{-1}(x)\). Reflect across the \(x\)-axis for \(y=-f^{-1}(x)\): \( (3,-1)\). Answer: \((3,-1)\).

Tangency at \(x=\pm5\) and leading coefficient 1 give \(P(x)=(x-5)^2(x+5)^2=(x^2-25)^2\). For exactly three intersections, \(y=k\) must pass through the central local maximum: \(k=P(0)=625\). Algebra: \(P(x)=625\Rightarrow(x^2-25)^2=625\Rightarrow x=-5\sqrt2,0,5\sqrt2\). The largest horizontal separation is \(10\sqrt2\). Answer: \(10\sqrt2\).

Domain exclusion: \(3x-1=0\Rightarrow k=1/3\). For the range, solve \(y=(2x+3)/(3x-1)\): \(x(3y-2)=y+3\). If \(y=2/3\), this becomes \(0=11/3\), impossible, so \(w=2/3\). Algebra: \(k+w=1/3+2/3=1\). Answer: \(1\).

Common points satisfy \(r=\theta=4/(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)\), hence \(\theta(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)=4\). Solving the intersections on \(0\le\theta\le8\pi\), the largest is \(d\approx24.4632\) (the preceding sign change is below this root). Algebra: \(\lfloor d\rfloor=\lfloor24.4632\rfloor=24\). Answer: \(24\).

Let \(h(x)=\cos(x/2)-\sin2x\). Then \(h'(x)=-\tfrac12\sin(x/2)-2\cos2x\). Solving \(h'(x)=0\) on \(0\le x\le\pi\) and comparing with the endpoints gives the maximum at \(x\approx2.24264\). Thus \(h(x)\approx1.408815\), so the answer is \(1.409\).

Since \(\sec x\ne0\) wherever it is defined, divide \(\sec x\,\csc^2x=2\sec x\) by \(\sec x\): \(\csc^2x=2\Rightarrow\sin^2x=1/2\). On \(0\le x<2\pi\), \(x=(2j+1)\pi/4\) for \(j=0,1,2,3\), so \(k=(2j+1)/4\). Their sum is \( (1+3+5+7)/4=4\). Answer: \(4\).

Let the double root be \(r\) and the third root be \(s\). Vieta: \(2r+s=-5\), \(k=r^2+2rs\), and \(r^2s=-6k\). Substitute \(s=-5-2r\): \(r^2s=-6(r^2+2rs)\Rightarrow2r^2+23r+60=0\), so \(r=-4\) or \(-15/2\). Integer coefficients select \(r=-4,s=3\), giving \(k=16-24=-8\), \(w=6k=-48\). Answer: \(k+w=-56\).

Reflection of a ray with angle \(\theta\) across a line of angle \(\alpha\) has angle \(2\alpha-\theta\). Substitution: \(0^\circ\to2(-12^\circ)=-24^\circ\to2(18^\circ)-(-24^\circ)=60^\circ\). Thus \(OP=OR=8\) and the angle between them is \(60^\circ\). Each altitude is \(8\sin60^\circ=4\sqrt3\). Answer: \(12\sqrt3\).

Sphere substitution with \(u=t^2\): \(t^2+t^4+t^6=100\Rightarrow u+u^2+u^3=100\). The two points use \(t=\pm\sqrt u\), so their dot product is \(-u+u^2-u^3\). Algebra: \(\cos\angle AOB=\dfrac{-u+u^2-u^3}{100}\), with \(u\approx4.26443\), giving \(\angle AOB\approx129.5^\circ\). Answer: \(129.5^\circ\).
Continuous compounding: \(A(t)=Ae^{0.055t}\). Set the target: \(Ae^{0.055t}=3A\Rightarrow e^{0.055t}=3\). Algebra: \(t=\dfrac{\ln3}{0.055}\approx19.97\) years. Answer: \(19.97\) years.

Let the minor central angle be \(\theta\). Equations: \(n=2r\sin(\theta/2)\) and \(n+1=r\theta\). Eliminate \(r\): \(2\sin(\theta/2)/\theta=n/(n+1)\). For \(n=1\) no minor-angle solution exists; the smallest possible integer is \(n=2\). Substitution: solve \(2\sin(\theta/2)/\theta=2/3\), giving \(\theta\approx2.991563\), then \(r=3/\theta\approx1.002820\). Answer: \(1.003\).

From the given sequence, \(f_{10}=55\), \(f_{11}=89\), so \(r_{10}=f_{11}/f_{10}=89/55\). The limit is \(L=\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\). Algebra: \(\lvert r_{10}-L\rvert=\left\lvert\dfrac{89}{55}-\dfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\right\rvert\approx0.0001478\). Answer: \(0.0001478\). The alternate keyed value \(0.00005646\) is \(\lvert r_{11}-L\rvert\), not the stated \(r_{10}\).
Binomial term equation: the fifth term has four factors of \(-2y\): \(T_5=\binom74(3x)^3(-2y)^4\). Algebra: the numerical coefficient is \(35\cdot27\cdot16=15120\). Answer: \(15120\).

Let \(x=AB\). Law of cosines: \(4^2=x^2+6^2-2(x)(6)\cos25^\circ\). Algebra: \(x^2-12x\cos25^\circ+20=0\), so \(x=6\cos25^\circ\pm\sqrt{16-36\sin^2 25^\circ}\). The smaller positive root is \(x\approx2.344\). Answer: \(2.344\).

Each new unit segment is perpendicular to the preceding radius, so \(OP_j^2=OP_{j-1}^2+1\). Substitution: \(OP_m^2=4^2+m=16+m\). The direction increment is \(\Delta_j=\arctan(1/\sqrt{16+j-1})\); summing gives \(\sum_{j=1}^{35}\Delta_j\approx6.26464\) (quadrant IV), while the next sum is \(6.40376\) (quadrant I). Thus \(m=35\). Algebra: \(OP_m=\sqrt{16+35}=\sqrt{51}\approx7.141\). Answer: \(7.141\).

Equation: \(|(a+bi)(c+di)|\). Substitution: \(|(a+bi)(c+di)|=\sqrt{(ac-bd)^2+(ad+bc)^2}\). Algebra: \((ac-bd)^2+(ad+bc)^2=(a^2+b^2)(c^2+d^2)\), so the modulus equals \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\sqrt{c^2+d^2}=|a+bi||c+di|\). Answer: Always.
Change of base: \(\log_\pi8=3\log_\pi2\), \(\log_{\sqrt3}\pi=2\log_3\pi\), and \(\tfrac12\log_2 3\) is the third factor. Algebra: \(k=3(\log_\pi2)(\log_3\pi)(\log_2 3)=3\). Answer: \(3\).

Compute dot products: \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=3(-8)+2(13)=2\), \(\vec a\cdot\vec c=3(16)+2(-24)=0\), and \(\vec b\cdot\vec c\ne0\). Thus \(\vec a\perp\vec c\). Algebra: \(\vec a+\vec c=(3,2)+(16,-24)=(19,-22)\). Answer: \((19,-22)\).
Equation: \(S=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(1/3)^n\). Geometric substitution: \(S=\dfrac{r}{1-r}\) with \(r=1/3\). Algebra: \(S=\dfrac{1/3}{1-1/3}=\dfrac12\). Answer: \(\dfrac12\).

The radii to tangency points are perpendicular to \(AB\) and \(BC\), so \(\angle EOF=\pi-B\), where \(B=\angle ABC\). Law of cosines: \(\cos B=\dfrac{8^2+10^2-12^2}{2(8)(10)}=1/8\). Algebra: \(\angle EOF=\pi-\arccos(1/8)\approx1.696\) radians. Answer: \(1.696\).

Since \(x^2+1\ge1\) and \(\operatorname{Arctan}\) is increasing, \(8\operatorname{Arctan}(x^2+1)\ge8\operatorname{Arctan}(1)\). Algebra: at \(x=0\), \(8\operatorname{Arctan}(1)=8(\pi/4)=2\pi\). Answer: \(2\pi\).

For \(n\) couples, handshake count is \(\binom n2+n(n-1)=\frac32n(n-1)\). Substitute 459: \(\frac32n(n-1)=459\Rightarrow n^2-n-306=0\Rightarrow(n-18)(n+17)=0\). Thus \(n=18\) couples, or \(36\) people. Answer: \(36\) people.
Continuity at \(x=3\) gives \(9a+3b+1=4\) and \(3a-b/2=4\). Algebra: \(3a+b=1\) and \(6a-b=8\); adding gives \(9a=9\Rightarrow a=1\), then \(b=-2\). Answer: \((1,-2)\).

Substitution: \(\sin^2(\theta/2)=(x-1)/(2x)\), so \(\cos\theta=1-2\sin^2(\theta/2)=1/x\). Algebra: \(\tan^2\theta=\dfrac{1-\cos^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=x^2-1\). Thus \(k=1,w=0,p=-1\), and \(k+w+p=0\). Answer: \(0\).
Equation: \(k=\lim_{x\to0}\left(1+\dfrac{\tan x}{x}\right)\). Substitution: \(\lim_{x\to0}\tan x/x=1\). Algebra: \(k=1+1=2\). Answer: \(2\).

Real coefficients and \(r_1-r_2=2i\) give roots \(r_1=u+i,r_2=u-i\). Substitute in the reciprocal condition: \(\dfrac{2u}{u^2+1}=3/5\Rightarrow3u^2-10u+3=0\Rightarrow u=3\text{ or }1/3\). For each \(u\), \(f(x)=x^2-2ux+(u^2+1)\), so \((k,w)=(-6,10)\) or \((-2/3,10/9)\). Algebra: total sum \(=-6+10-2/3+10/9=40/9\). Answer: \(40/9\).

The midline is \(5+10=15\) and the angular speed is \(2\pi/30=\pi/15\). Since the point starts at its minimum, \(h(t)=15-10\cos(\pi t/15)\). Substitution: \(h(17)=15-10\cos(17\pi/15)\approx24.135\). Answer: \(24.135\) meters.

Match \(a\sin(4x+c)=a\cos c\sin4x+a\sin c\cos4x\) with \(5\sin4x+2\cos4x\). Substitution: \(a\cos c=5\), \(a\sin c=2\), so \(a^2=25+4=29\Rightarrow a=\sqrt{29}\), and \(b=4\). Algebra: \(a+b=\sqrt{29}+4\). Answer: \(4+\sqrt{29}\).
Equation: \(720/n!=6\). Algebra: \(n!=720/6=120=5!\), so the positive integer is \(n=5\). Answer: \(5\).

Let \(\alpha=\angle BAC=\angle CAD=\angle DAE\), and set \(AB=b,AC=c\). Angle-bisector theorem: \(AD/AB=CD/BC=3/2\Rightarrow AD=3b/2\), and \(AE/AC=DE/CD=2\Rightarrow AE=2c\). Cosine law in the three small triangles gives \(b^2+c^2-2bc\cos\alpha=4\), \(9b^2/4+c^2-3bc\cos\alpha=9\), and \(9b^2/4+4c^2-6bc\cos\alpha=36\). Algebraic elimination yields \(b^2=40,c^2=54\), so \(AB=2\sqrt{10},AC=3\sqrt6\). Therefore \(P=2+2\sqrt{10}+3\sqrt6\), and \(f+k+w+p+q=2+2+10+3+6=23\). Answer: \(23\).

Convert the polar equation: \(r=4/(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)\Rightarrow r\sin\theta+r\cos\theta=4\). Substitution \(x=r\cos\theta,y=r\sin\theta\) gives \(x+y=4\). On \(0\le\theta\le\pi/2\), the segment runs from \((4,0)\) to \((0,4)\). Algebra: its length is \(\sqrt{(4-0)^2+(0-4)^2}=4\sqrt2\). Answer: \(4\sqrt2\).

Substitute \(x=-2+t,y=at,z=b+ct\) into \(x+y-z=0\): constants give \(b=-2\), and coefficients give \(1+a-c=0\). The first plane gives \(-4+2b+(2-4a+2c)t=-8\), so \(1-2a+c=0\). Solving yields \(a=2,b=-2,c=3\), hence \(a+b+c=3\). Answer: \(3\).

Euler's formula gives \(e^{ki\pi}=\cos(k\pi)+i\sin(k\pi)\). For real \(k\), this is nonreal whenever \(k\notin\mathbb Z\), so as written there is no smallest positive value of \(12k-100\). The keyed answer \(2\) requires the unstated intended restriction that \(k\) be a half-integer; then the least \(k>100/12=25/3\) is \(17/2\), giving \(12k-100=2\).
